column1: # Every page in Claude Code's documentation index, as of the snapshot date.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `build-parity-report.py` used to treat any cited
# `<name>.md` as a Claude page. It is not: this repo also cites Codex's plugin
# `build-plugins.md`), the MCP spec (`elicitation.md`), and assorted names that
# are neither (`cmd.md`, `react.md`, `style.md`). All of them landed in a table
# headed "By Claude's documentation", which made that axis unusable as a
# coverage map — a reviewer could not tell a Claude contract from a Codex one.
# This file is the allowlist that separates them, and it is also the DENOMINATOR:
# a coverage map needs the pages we never cited, and only a full page list has
# NOTE: refresh-claude-doc-pages.py emits DATA ONLY — it strips this header.
# Re-add it after regenerating (measured 2026-08-09: the documented command
# silently deleted all 24 comment lines, including this warning).
# REGENERATE when Claude's docs change (new pages are the recurring failure mode
# — see AGENTS.md, "Renames and new component types"):
# CHECKS A REFRESH RE-RUNS. A refreshed corpus can change a page's CONTENT
# without changing this file's data rows at all, so the page tables this repo
# transcribes have to be re-read by hand. The ones with a test that names the
# page sentence it pins, run them after every refresh:
#     combination rules (three bullets when first quoted here, six now), and
#     managed-settings.md#keys-that-fail-closed — the ten enforcement keys plus
#     the two the closing sentence exempts, one case each (P6.251).
# A PAGE SPLIT is the failure mode a page count cannot show. Measured 2026-08-25:
# `settings` is no longer the key-by-key reference this repo quotes as
# `settings.md:<line>`. It is now scope/precedence/how-to-edit (804 lines, and its
# first ~460 lines are a React component), and the material split three ways:
#   settings             — precedence, scope, editing, "Lists merge instead of
#   settings-reference   — every key, one section per key (5 474 lines)
#   managed-settings     — deploying a policy, and the invalid-value behaviour
#                          table ("Keys that fail closed") this repo enforces
# THE COUNT IS A READING WITH A DATE — run the census, never quote a number from
# this header. The command is the one AGENTS.md carries (its "A page can SPLIT"
# bullet), byte-honest because `git grep` reads bytes and `-a` does not skip the
# NUL-carrying files a plain `grep` drops silently; a wrapped `grep -r` walks
#   git grep -ahoI -E "$R" | wc -l && git grep -ahoI -E "$R" | sort -u | wc -l
# MEASURE AT A REF, NOT THE WORKING TREE (measured 2026-09-07, `P6.657`). The same
# command over the dirty tree printed 840, 841 and 843 in three runs minutes apart,
# because sibling lanes were committing docs that carry these citations. Pass the
# sha — `git grep -ahoI -E "$R" <sha>` — and record it beside the number, or the
# census measures the wave instead of the tree.
# is included, **840** counting the four `managed-settings.md:<line>` as well, over
# **140** distinct anchor strings. This header said 767/835 on 2026-08-29, the plan
# said 772, another pass said 828, and a 2026-09-07 pass over a different tree state
# said 754/822 — every one correct when written, which is the whole point. Where the
# 771 sit, because the bucket decides whether a conversion is worth doing at all:
#     265  packages/  source comments        <- a reader follows these
#      16  apps/      source comments        <- a reader follows these
#       6  docs/ live                        <- a reader follows these
# So 287 of the 771 are followable and 484 are frozen evidence, where rewriting an
# anchor would falsify the record of what a dated pass actually cited. Convert the
# followable ones to `page.md#<section>` plus the verbatim sentence; leave the frozen
# ones and say why, rather than reporting the whole 771 as a backlog. WHICH of them
# are worth converting, which are deliberately frozen, and the rendered-verified
# successor anchor plus today's verbatim sentence for the most-cited ones:
# All three were absent or wrong somewhere when that was measured: two of them
# were missing from THIS file entirely, so `check-coverage-map.ts` was validating
# a corpus with a hole in it, and AGENTS.md pointed the plugin-format contract
# list at the page that had stopped holding the contract. A count going 186 → 191
# looks like five additions; it was also one page becoming three.
# Re-verified 2026-08-28 against a fresh `llms.txt`: the page SET is identical, 191 = 191,
# nothing entered or left. Recorded because the coverage map and the parity report both read
# this file as their denominator, and a denominator nobody re-checks is the one number a
# staleness gate cannot catch — `--check` on either generator compares outputs, not corpora.
# 2026-10-17 (UB12.95): 210 → 228, nothing left. Joined: the ten `plugins/mods/*` pages (a
# mod is a plugin whose `hooks/hooks.json` names a `modules` path), six `code-review-*` pages,
# `auto-mode-classifier-billing` and `hipaa-setup`. The six are a SPLIT, the failure a count
# cannot show: `code-review` is now the cloud service, and two of the sections this repo cites
# moved to `code-review-local`, the local `/code-review` page. The index also began listing
# 36 pages twice (264 links over 228 slugs, same titles), so the refresh script now writes
